clue.text: Posts and planks will be about fifty pounds

indicators.note: about means going round, so the planks word encloses the two letters

parts.note: planks are boards
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A timber merchant warns that the planks will cost around fifty pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L and L inside BOARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Short stout posts set in a road or on a quay are a synonym here.

clue.text: Cook given lift from Birkenhead

indicators.note: from here means taking the head, the opening letter, of Birkenhead

parts.note: to lift is to raise

explanation.surface: A cook gets a promotion from the Birkenhead branch.
explanation.walkthrough: Birkenhead is a town on Merseyside; its 'head' is B.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew slowly in a little liquid in a closed pot is a way to cook.

clue.text: More off for instruction?

parts.note: more off means ..., and the two words joined make a word for a teaching session

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to remove more clothing on instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A period of teaching is an instruction session.

clue.text: Naval type redeployed mad liar

indicators.note: redeployed means arranged anew, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A crazy liar is posted elsewhere in the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeployed' rearranges MAD LIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag officer of high rank in a fleet is a naval type.

clue.text: A hand-out for distress

definitions.meaning: a share given out, or British state unemployment benefit
an old literary word for grief or sorrow

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both benefit money handed out by the state and, archaically, grief.

clue.text: Part of the four o'clock service?

definitions.text: Part of the four o'clock service?

parts.words: Part of the four o'clock service?
parts.note: service reads as a church service at four, but means a tea service, the china set laid out for afternoon tea, and one cup of it is the item

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which section of a mid-afternoon church service is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four o'clock' is the British teatime; a 'service' is a matching set of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set is a service, and the small cup for drinking from is one piece of that set.

clue.text: Makes a mistake, also put in for commissions

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: errs means makes a mistake
and means also

explanation.surface: Someone blunders and also applies for commissions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' is the container signal; the comma after 'mistake' hides that 'also' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Small tasks one is sent out to do are commissions.

clue.text: Polite Scotsman — not a soldier

parts.note: civil means polite
Ian is the Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: A courteous Scot turns out not to be in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A person not in the armed forces is a non-soldier.

clue.text: Spoils part of the book about the sick

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: pages are part of a book
the ill are the sick

explanation.surface: Part of a book about sick people is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'Spoils' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder or loot is to strip of spoils.

clue.text: May bless conversion congregation of congregation

indicators.note: conversion turns one thing into another, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious conversion may bring blessing to a church gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' rearranges MAY BLESS. The clue as held repeats 'congregation'; the second one is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people, such as a body of worshippers, is a synonym.

clue.text: He leaves the composer to move on

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so these two letters drop out of the phrase

parts.note: the composer is THE plus Ravel, the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: A man walks out on the composer and moves on with his life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes HE out of THE RAVEL, leaving T plus RAVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To journey from place to place is to move on.

clue.text: They won't let us have material with advertisements

definitions.meaning: people who forbid things, those who ban

explanation.definitionFit: The word reads as forbidders, people who ban, and also means cloth placards bearing slogans or adverts.

clue.text: Seeks hard to achieve cleanliness

definitions.meaning: searches a place thoroughly, combing every corner
rubs a surface hard with an abrasive to make it clean

explanation.surface: Someone scrubs away hard in pursuit of a spotless home.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two senses: searching an area thoroughly, and scrubbing a pan clean with something rough.

clue.text: In a loam compost force this shrub

indicators.note: compost is a mixture, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: g is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a shrub in loamy compost and forces it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compost' mixes IN, A, LOAM and G. 'Compost' looks like part of the gardening picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering tree or bush with large showy blooms is an example of a shrub.

clue.text: Thinks well of both sire and dam

indicators.note: both throws the two words together, mixing their letters as one pool

explanation.surface: A breeder thinks highly of both the father and mother of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: SIRE and DAM are a horse's father and mother; their letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard with approval is to think well of.

clue.text: Selling a disc? Work out price variation

indicators.note: work out suggests solving or reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A record dealer tries to calculate how prices should shift when selling a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' rearranges SELLING A DISC.
explanation.definitionFit: A system where charges or rates rise and fall with some other factor is a price variation.

clue.text: Declare prime coal production not easy at first

indicators.note: production means making something new, so these letters are reworked
not marks a letter missing from the rearranged pool
at first takes the opening letter of easy

explanation.surface: An official announces that producing top-grade coal is hard at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges PRIME COAL less E, from 'easy' with 'at first'; 'not' signals the E is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce publicly is to declare.

clue.text: Could be set in arc, but has less fullness than most

indicators.note: could be means the letters might form another word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An object placed in an arc turns out to be thinner than most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges SET IN ARC.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaner or skimpier things have less fullness.

clue.text: Sorted out clatter in car — someone kicking against the brake

indicators.note: sorted out means put in order differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic fixes a rattle in the car, while the driver fights the brake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' rearranges CLATTER IN CAR. The definition plays on 'kicking against the pricks', resisting authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A stubbornly defiant person resists restraint, like a horse kicking against a brake.

clue.text: Staying? Or going on and on?

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means durable and enduring, so both remaining and continuing long.

clue.text: Most run wild, to be specific

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run into a new order

explanation.surface: Most people run wild to make a particular point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges MOST RUN. A 'specific' is an old noun for a remedy for one disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy or cure-all medicine is a specific in the old medical sense.

clue.text: Result of over-production in French wheat extract

parts.note: a glut is an oversupply caused by producing too much
en is French for in

explanation.surface: A French wheat product results from overproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: The protein left when starch is washed out of wheat flour is an extract of wheat.

clue.text: Measure the corpse then join together in a mass

parts.note: an em is a printer's measure of width
a body is a corpse

explanation.surface: An undertaker measures the corpse before assembling the mourners.
explanation.definitionFit: To incorporate or unite things into a whole is to join them in a mass.

clue.text: Tobacco leaves may flower?

parts.note: may in the sense of being able, as can
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether tobacco leaves might bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' joins the definition to the wordplay, as in 'Tobacco yields'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse kind of tobacco originally shipped in rush baskets is an example of the word.

clue.text: Provides relief in easy lump sum payments

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Lump sum payments are offered to ease someone's hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across eASY LUMp.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge or sanctuary is a place offering relief and protection.

clue.text: Hard fish to skin

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Tough fish is difficult to skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's pelt is its skin.

clue.text: A student seen with a bird claims to have been elsewhere

parts.note: L is a learner, the plate on a student driver's car
an ibis is a long-billed wading bird

explanation.surface: A student spotted with a bird insists they were somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner is the British plate shown by a learner driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Excuses that the accused was somewhere other than the crime scene are such claims.

clue.text: After small party, fur returned — needed by diva

parts.note: the Liberals, shortened to Lib, were a small British political party

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: otter is a fur from the river animal

explanation.surface: After a little party, a fur coat is sent back, as the diva requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the fur backwards; Lib was the usual short form for the Liberal Party, then small.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera singer needs the text of the opera, the words she sings.

clue.text: Motorway madness a delusion?

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
rage is fury or madness

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether road rage on the motorway is all in the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; crosswords read the digit 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion, such as water seen on a hot road, is a kind of delusion.

clue.text: Gay men co-translated earth-shaking predictions

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some men jointly translate startling prophecies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges GAY MEN CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Divination using figures of earth or marks on the ground is a form of predicting.
